tasks.instruction:
Update glom.core so nested specifications behave consistently across all supported spec types and argument forms. Dot-delimited paths must navigate nested mappings and attributes, T expressions must resolve against the current target, and S expressions must resolve scope variables. Callable invocations must resolve each positional and keyword argument according to the same spec rules, including zero, one, and multiple arguments, without special-casing particular argument counts; literal values must remain usable through the repository’s established constant mechanism.

Spec wrappers must recursively evaluate their contained specifications. Match and Switch must evaluate their fallback/default specifications when no case matches. Assign must evaluate its assigned value as a specification, support values derived from T expressions and scope variables, and make assignments available through the appropriate subsequent scope/target lookups. T-derived subspecs and S-derived scope assignments must compose correctly with nested specs, recursion, path traversal, and callable invocation.

All supported combinations must produce the expected transformed value rather than leaving a spec object unevaluated or treating a spec as an unintended constant. Missing paths, failed matches, invalid calls, and other evaluation failures must retain the project’s exception types and report useful formatted context, including the relevant operation/path, while explicit defaults continue to handle only the cases they are intended to handle.
tasks.title: Make nested glom specifications and arguments evaluate consistently
